headline: The tidiest team in the league
summary: You've left 16.5 points on your bench all season, the lowest in the league by some distance, and you're 2–0. That's real management, not luck — though your 'vs. everyone' record of 6–8 says the schedule has helped too. Your one genuine problem is receiver depth: you're starting one ranked WR47, and one of your bench spots has been dead all season.

waivers.why: Justin Jefferson left Sunday with an ankle injury and Addison steps straight into the number one role — he already cashed it in for a 41-yard touchdown. You're starting Makai Lemon (WR47) and your other options are Michael Pittman Jr. and Travis Hunter. This is your upgrade, and A.J. Brown is your free roster spot.
waivers.stat: Ranked WR50 for the rest of the season, set before Jefferson got hurt. Heavily targeted on Sunday including a 41-yard score.

waivers.why: Ranked WR34, well above what you're currently starting, and available. The catch is he's been quiet all season and his quarterback just dislocated a thumb, so this is depth rather than a fix.
waivers.stat: 3 catches for 25 yards on Sunday. Ranked WR34.

start_sit.why: Conditional on one thing: Garrett Wilson left Sunday's game with an injury on the final drive. If he's limited, Warren is the play — he ran for 127 yards at 7.5 a carry, the back ahead of him is OUT with a toe injury, and his team plays Thursday, so you'll know early. If Wilson is cleared and healthy, keep him in; he did just catch 10 of 13 for 107 yards and a touchdown.

watch.note: On injured reserve and has been for all three weeks. That roster spot has never done anything for you. Drop him.
Exited on the final drive with an injury. Check his status early in the week — this is the one thing that could cost you week 4.
Questionable with a shoulder, but practised all week and expected to play. Thursday game, so decide early.
Questionable with a foot, and the advice is to avoid him this week regardless. Leave him benched.

trade_ideas.why: She'll probably say no — Fannin is ranked TE9 and Pitts TE13 — but she's asked around for tight end help and you have Tyler Warren starting anyway. If she'll add a receiver to even it up, that's your depth problem solved.

your_habits.title: Best lineup setter
your_habits.text: 16.5 points benched in two weeks, and never more than 8.5 in a single week. Nobody else is close.

your_habits.title: Thin at receiver
your_habits.text: You're 2–0 while starting a receiver ranked WR47 and holding a player who's been on injured reserve since week 1. One claim fixes both.

glossary.def: The wild-card starting spot — fill it with a running back, receiver or tight end, whoever you expect to score most.
Where long-term injuries go. A player on IR isn't playing, so holding one costs you a roster spot for nothing.
Your request for an unrostered player. Claims process on Wednesday; if two people want the same player, waiver order decides.
Some weeks start Thursday night. If your player is in that game, your lineup decision is due days earlier than usual.
